To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a customer base analysis to determine a customer's profile is not necessarily an accurate way to predict that customer's behavior and that (2) the use of behavioral data in a customer-base analysis is not an appropriate way to predict a customer's future behavior.

(i) the use of a customer-base analysis (CBA) model to estimate the effects of a behavioral targeting (BT) program can be misleading if the model is not properly specified and (ii) a CBA model should be specified to include a user-profiling variable to account for differences in the effectiveness of BT across different user segments.
the use of user profiling in customer-base analysis and behavioral targeting is a promising area for future research.
